lessons.title: Frame the problem and make a useful sketch
lessons.objective: Create a labeled sketch or equivalent text diagram, define the system boundary and unknown, and separate supplied facts from modeling assumptions.
scope: Boundary, components, flow or direction, symbols and units
Model limitations and an actionable missing-information question
examples: Travel-time sketch with a stated positive direction and one unknown
Data-buffer block diagram with channels, sampling rate and storage boundary
Filling-volume sketch with initial state and inflow
Repair a diagram that labels numbers but omits their meanings
lessons.guided: Annotate a supplied buffer scenario with knowns, an unknown, boundary and one assumption.
lessons.activity: Editable problem frame and diagram description; compare against a possible review only after attempting, then revise.
fields: Labeled sketch or equivalent text diagram
rubric: boundary
I named what is inside and outside the model and the requested output.
labels
My sketch or text diagram labels connections or directions, symbols and units.
assumptions
I separated stated facts from assumptions and named a useful question.

diagnostic.prompt: A page says 12, 3 and 4 beside an unlabeled box. What should you do before choosing an equation?
options: Name the quantities, units, boundary and unknown
Labels connect the picture to a physical model.
Arithmetic cannot supply missing meanings or a requested output.
Visual detail does not replace useful labels.

mistakes: Equation chosen before the unknown is defined
State the output and model boundary first.
Attach symbol meanings, units and directions.
Mark assumptions and explain when they could fail.

lessons.title: Estimate first and carry units through the model
lessons.objective: Record a rough prediction before detailed calculation, use a dimensionally consistent relationship, and explain how one uncertain input changes the result.
scope: A justified equation with units on every input and result
Explicit unit conversion and sensible reporting precision
One-at-a-time sensitivity as a model check, not an uncertainty distribution
examples: Travel time estimated before a distance/speed calculation
Buffer size from channels times sample rate times duration times bytes
Fill duration with litres and litres per minute
Compare two plausible rates and report a range rather than false precision
lessons.guided: Write a rough storage estimate, carry units through the product, then double the duration and predict its effect.
lessons.activity: Seeded estimate worksheet with separate pre-calculation prediction, unit audit and sensitivity fields; reveal comparison marks the record assisted.
fields: One changed input and the predicted effect
rubric: estimate
I wrote a rough expectation before the detailed result.
units
My relationship and conversions carry units consistently.
sensitivity
I checked one input change and avoided unsupported precision.

diagnostic.prompt: You want travel time from 12 km and 4 km/h. Which relationship has the right meaning and units?
options: km divided by km/h gives hours.
That has units km²/h, not time.

mistakes: Treating physical quantities as bare numbers
Keep conversion factors and units visible.
Report precision justified by the data and assumptions.

lessons.title: Check reasonableness and model limits
lessons.objective: Audit a result with independent checks of dimensions, sign, scale and limiting behavior, identify the first unsupported step, and explain what remains uncertain.
scope: Correct dimensions are necessary but not sufficient
Sign/direction, estimate comparison, zero or doubled-input behavior
Independent reconstruction and data versus model mismatch
Repair the first cause and retain uncertainty
examples: A unit-correct travel result is still off by a factor of 60
A buffer formula omits its channel factor
A fill-time formula reverses rate and volume
A measured result differs from a constant-rate model
lessons.guided: Audit a flawed buffer solution with a channel omission; distinguish a dimension check from a value check.
lessons.activity: Seeded flawed-report audit; record the first error, independent checks, correction and a model limitation before revealing reference reasoning.
fields: Dimension, sign, scale, and limit checks
rubric: checks
I used more than one independent check, including units and scale or limiting behavior.
cause
I identified a cause instead of changing an unexplained final number.
limits
I verified the correction and stated a limit of the model.

diagnostic.prompt: A storage calculation has units of bytes but forgot the number of channels. What does the unit check establish?
options: It checks dimensions but does not prove the value
A missing dimensionless channel count can preserve units and change the result.
Correct units alone do not establish numerical or model correctness.
The answer must have the wrong dimensions
The omitted factor is dimensionless, so this claim is too strong.

mistakes: Units used as the only check
Add a scale, limiting-case or reconstruction check.
Final number patched without a cause
Find the first divergence and recompute from there.
Check both observations and simplifying assumptions.

lessons.title: Revise and leave a reproducible work record
lessons.objective: Preserve an initial attempt, document a specific evidence-based revision, and produce a concise final record with inputs, method, result, checks and next action.
scope: Before/after reasoning and why a change is warranted
Independent practical task with rubric; self-check evidence not automatic mastery
examples: Correct a minutes-to-hours conversion while preserving the original
Revise a buffer assumption from one channel to three
Update a fill model after observed rate changes
Write a handoff paragraph with result, checks, assumptions and next measurement
lessons.guided: Turn a flawed short report into a revision log and a reproducible final explanation.
lessons.activity: Save a draft, retain a completed artifact, start a fresh scenario and revise without erasing the last completed record. Assistance remains labeled when a reference is revealed.
fields: Original attempt and what prompted review
Specific change and the evidence for it
rubric: history
I retained the original claim and explained the revision.
reproduce
Another learner can reconstruct my inputs, units, method and result.
next
I recorded an independent check, a model limitation and a concrete next action.

diagnostic.prompt: Your corrected answer differs from yesterday's. What makes the revision useful to a future reader?
options: Keep the earlier claim and explain the corrected step and checks
A revision log preserves the reason for the change.
Erase the earlier result and keep only the new number
That hides what changed and why the new result is more trustworthy.
Write that you are now very confident
Confidence is not a record of evidence or method.

mistakes: Only the final number is saved
Treating the answer as the whole solution
Preserve inputs, method, units, checks and assumptions.
Record the cause and before/after reasoning.
Label practical completion, assistance and human-review limits explicitly.
